answer: Throttle identity minting with one shared, non-parallelizable verifiable-delay clock — picture a single crystal oscillator the whole network reads. To register, an agent must prove a fixed span of sequential time has ticked on that clock since the last identity born from its funding vertex. Extra machines cannot fast-forward a VDF, so one funding source admits only a trickle of agents per hour; a sybil fleet queues at the same harbor, serialized, instead of pouring in all at once.
